backpacks.description:
RL/LG backpack drops: time, dropper, weapon (rl/lg), origin XYZ (the pack's own position, 24 units below the victim's origin) and resolved loc. Each row names its provenance in `source`, and the two are never mixed within one demo:

  * `ktx` — decoded from KTX's `//ktx drop` hint. `entNum` is the
    hinted edict and joins to WeaponPickup.backpackEnt; since schema
    v77 that join is already on the row: `fate: picked` with
    `picker`/`pickerTeam`/`pickupTime` and the pickup's
    `pickerHadWeapon`/`pickerKills`/`pickerNextDeathTime`. `expired`
    when KTX announced the 120 s removal in `//ktx expire`,
    `unobserved` when neither hint names the pack (NOT "nobody took
    it").
  * `reconstructed` — replayed from the server's own drop rule on a
    demo whose mod never hinted. There is no pickup hint to join to,
    so the pickup side is carried on the row itself (schema v72):
    `fate` (`picked`/`expired`/`unobserved`) plus `pickupTime` and
    `picker`/`pickerTeam` when the wire named one, read off the
    bound backpack entity — whose edict number `entNum` now carries
    as well. A `reconstructed` `entNum` still joins to nothing;
    it identifies the pack track, not a pickup row. The three
    `ktx`-only pickup figures are absent here.

Every row naming a `picker` carries `pickerRelation` (`self` / `team` / `enemy`, relative to the dropper), so "packs the enemy took" is `pickerRelation == enemy`.
Always 200 — empty when none, which means either no pack dropped or the reconstruction stood down; the wire shape does not distinguish the two.

from.description: Window start, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no lower bound. Endpoints treat the window as inclusive on both ends. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

label.description: Non-secret traffic-source tag for access-log attribution. Accepted on every endpoint; never affects the response.

players.description: CSV of player display names. Case-SENSITIVE (QW names are case-significant). Omit for all players. Filter semantics are per-endpoint (e.g. killer-or-victim on /frags, speaker on /chat).

to.description: Window end, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no upper bound. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

weapon.description: Deprecated legacy alias of `weapons` (the pre-16.2 singular spelling). Ignored when `weapons` is present.

weapons.description:
CSV of weapon codes (case-insensitive). Core codes: rl, lg, gl, ssg,
sng, ng, sg, axe; on /damage the pseudo-codes tele/stomp select the
positional instant kills (which carry no real weapon).

Each endpoint validates against its OWN closed vocabulary and returns
400 `invalid_param` (listing the valid set) for an unknown token — no
more silent empty result:

- **/backpacks** accepts rl/lg only;

`water` and `drown` are the SAME cause under the two logs' different
spellings and are accepted interchangeably wherever either is valid,
so you need not know which log backs the endpoint you are calling.

The pre-16.2 singular spelling `weapon` is an accepted legacy alias;
`weapons` wins when both are present.

entNum.description: Server entity/edict number — stable id within a match. On a `ktx` row it comes from the wire hint and joins to WeaponPickup.backpackEnt. On a `reconstructed` row it is the backpack-model entity the linkage bound to the drop and joins to nothing (that row's pickup side is `fate`/`picker` below). 0 means no entity was identified; never treat 0 as an edict.

fate.description:
What the wire showed happening to the pack (schema v72). `picked` — the pack entity left the wire with a live player's bounding box overlapping it, the same test the server runs before BackpackTouch; `pickupTime` is when, and `picker` is set only when the evidence named exactly one player. `expired` — SUB_Remove took it at KTX's 120 s timeout, untaken: the one outcome that is positively not a pickup. `unobserved` — no entity bound to the drop, or it was still on the wire when the recording stopped, or it left early with nobody on it; none of which is evidence that nobody took the pack.
A `reconstructed` row can carry any of the three, read off the backpack-entity track. A `ktx` row (schema v77) is `picked` when the `//ktx bp` pickup on /weapon-pickups joined to it (entNum + drop time — the picker fields below are copied from that row), `expired` when KTX said so in `//ktx expire <ent>`, and `unobserved` otherwise: a demo can carry the drop hint and no pickup hints at all, so no `//ktx bp` is not evidence that nobody took it. Read `source` for a `fate`'s provenance, exactly as for the row. On reconstructed rows, measured against the hints withheld: 223 demos, 100.00% precision and 96.13% recall on picked-vs-not, 99.98% of named pickers correct.

loc.description: Nearest named location from the map .loc file.

picker.description: Who took the pack (schema v72). Set only with `fate: picked`, and only when the evidence named exactly ONE player — two players on one pack with nothing to separate them leave this empty rather than guess. On a `ktx` row, the `//ktx bp` pickup's player (schema v77; reconstructed rows since v72).

pickerHadWeapon.description: Whether the picker already held the pack's weapon — the joined /weapon-pickups row's `hadBefore` (schema v77). `ktx` rows only: the entity track a reconstructed pickup is read from cannot say.

pickerKills.description: Kills credited to this pickup — the joined /weapon-pickups row's `kills` (0 when the picker already held the weapon; schema v77). `ktx` rows only.

pickerNextDeathTime.description: The picker's next death, int32 ms since match start — the joined /weapon-pickups row's `nextDeathTime`; absent if they never died again (schema v77). `ktx` rows only.

pickerRelation.description: The picker's side relative to the dropper (schema v77): `self` when the dropper respawned and took their own pack back, `team` when both carry the same team, else `enemy` — in a duel or FFA every other picker is an enemy. Set whenever `picker` is.

pickerTeam.description: Team of `picker`. Omitted when the picker has no team — an FFA or duel picker is named with no `pickerTeam`, so read its absence as "teamless", not as "no picker". Set with `picker` (reconstructed rows since v72, `ktx` rows since v77).

pickupTime.description: When the pack left the wire, int32 ms since match start. Set with `fate: picked` (with or without a `picker`; reconstructed rows since v72, `ktx` rows since v77).

source.description: Where this row came from (schema v72). `ktx` — decoded from KTX's `//ktx drop` hint, which fires exactly once per real pack and is emitted only by KTX >= 1.38 (49% of the archive). `reconstructed` — replayed from DropBackpack's own rule (the victim's wielded weapon at the death instant, dropped at their last broadcast position) on a demo whose mod never hinted. The two are never mixed within one demo; a reconstructed section stands down entirely rather than guess where the evidence is unmeasurable.

time.description: Event/sample time, int32 ms since match start.

events.description:
Discrete match events (frags, spawns, pickups, powerups, streaks,
chat, demo markers, …) in one time-ordered list. `detail` is
polymorphic per event type. Omit `types` for the default set
(includes `pickup`, `demomark`, `airgib`, `discharge`, `quadbore`, and `pause`).

Three event types worth spelling out:

- **`demomark`** events are the bookmarks players insert in-game with
  `/demomark`; a warmup mark carries a negative `time`, and a mark
  inserted by a spectator carries `detail.spectator: true`.
- **`airgib`** events are direct enemy rocket hits landed on an
  airborne victim (the Key Moments highlight list): `player` is the
  attacker (rocketeer) and `detail` carries `victim`,
  `attackerTeam?`/`victimTeam?`, `height` (victim feet above the floor
  at the hit), `heightAboveAttacker?`, `loc?`, `damage` (raw), and
  `lethal: true` when the hit killed.
- **`discharge`** / **`quadbore`** events (in the default set, like
  `airgib` — the `frag` event carries only the score delta, so
  nothing else in the feed says a death was a discharge) are the
  highlight-catalogue kinds: `player` is the actor and `detail`
  carries `victims` (names), `enemyKills`, `teamKills`,
  `actorKilled?`, `damage?`, `team?`, plus `cells?` on a discharge
  and `weapon`, `quadHeldMs`, `quadFrags` on a quadbore. The full
  rows with every participant's state are `/highlights`.
- **`pause`** events mark a game-clock freeze segment and carry NO
  `player` (so a `players=` filter excludes them);
  `detail.durationMs` is the real wall-clock ms the pause consumed.

from.description: Window start, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no lower bound. Endpoints treat the window as inclusive on both ends. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

label.description: Non-secret traffic-source tag for access-log attribution. Accepted on every endpoint; never affects the response.

loc.description: Loc rendering — `name` (default) resolves loc indices to names; `index` returns raw LocTable indices (decode via /loc-table).

players.description: CSV of player display names. Case-SENSITIVE (QW names are case-significant). Omit for all players. Filter semantics are per-endpoint (e.g. killer-or-victim on /frags, speaker on /chat).

to.description: Window end, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no upper bound. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

types.description: CSV of event types: frag, powerup, streak, spawn, death, weapon, item, chat, pickup, demomark, airgib, discharge, quadbore, pause (the default set), plus the opt-in high-frequency / dedicated lenses damage, health, armor, loc, telefrag, stomp. Omit for the default set. An unknown type value 400s (invalid_param) rather than silently matching nothing.

detail.actorKilled.description: discharge/quadbore: the actor died in the event.

detail.bounded.description: KTX-scoreboard bounded value — on damage events the stored per-hit reconstruction (present only when it differs from the raw damage), on telefrag/stomp events the reconstructed kill value; absent when the bounded reconstruction was skipped; 0 is a real value.

detail.cells.description: discharge: the discharger's cells before firing (35 × cells radius damage).

detail.damage.description: Raw/unbound wire damage amount, including overkill (see bounded for the KTX-scoreboard value).

detail.durationMs.description: pause real wall-clock ms consumed (pause events).

detail.entNum.description: Server entity/edict number — stable id within a match.

detail.height.description: airgib victim feet above the floor at the hit (units).

detail.heightAboveAttacker.description: airgib victim origin minus shooter origin at the hit (units; negative = victim below shooter); omitted when 0.

detail.lethal.description: airgib hit killed the victim (matching rocket frag near the hit).

detail.loc.description: Nearest named location from the map .loc file.

detail.quadFrags.description: quadbore: the actor's kills in that quad run before the bore.

detail.quadHeldMs.description: quadbore: ms since the quad pickup when the actor died.

detail.victimWep.description: Victim weapon class at hit time.

detail.victims.description: discharge/quadbore: names of everyone else the event touched (killed or hurt).

highlights.description:
The stored highlight catalogue (`highlights`): every LG water discharge, every quadbore (self-kill by own rocket/grenade while holding quad), every telefrag (incl. the pentagram deflections and spawnicides) and every airgib, as four lists of one row shape. Each row carries an `actor`, its `victims`, enemy/team kill counters, the damage-log figure and the evidence `sources`; every participant carries their relation to the actor and their state read one millisecond before the event — health, armor (+ type), stack, weapons, wielded weapon, powerups, loc — so toplists are a client-side sort (discharges by `enemyKills`/`damage`/`cells`, quadbores by `quadHeldMs` ascending against KTX's 30 s quad, telefrags by `victims[0].stack`, airgibs by `heightAboveAttacker`).

All four lists are always present — `[]` when the match had none or `kinds` excluded them; `kinds` echoes the filter. `players` keeps rows whose actor or a victim is named. `preMs` re-runs only the airgib detection. 422 `highlights_unavailable` when the demo has no match streams or no frag log to build the catalogue from.

kinds.description: CSV of highlight kinds to keep: discharge, quadbore, telefrag, airgib. Omit for all four. The unrequested lists still come back, empty; the envelope's `kinds` echoes what applied. An unknown kind 400s (invalid_param).

label.description: Non-secret traffic-source tag for access-log attribution. Accepted on every endpoint; never affects the response.

players.description: CSV of player display names. Case-SENSITIVE (QW names are case-significant). Omit for all players. Filter semantics are per-endpoint (e.g. killer-or-victim on /frags, speaker on /chat).

preMs.description: Pre-hit look-back in MILLISECONDS: every position sample in the window [hit-preMs, hit-40ms] must read at or above the airborne height threshold; the tick preceding the window decides when the window holds no sample near its start (old coarse-tick demos, recording holes), and a grounded reading beside the hit vetoes. Values at or below 40 collapse to a point check at the pre-impact boundary. Default 100. The gate exists because the KTX damage entry is stamped at (or one frame after) the physics frame in which the rocket's own knockback already moved the victim, so the sample nearest the damage time reports players who were STANDING at impact as hundreds of units airborne. `preMs=0` turns the pre-hit gate off (hit-time sample only, the pre-v73 detection); values above 1000 are rejected with 400 `invalid_param`, since a look-back that long lands before the flight that made the hit an airgib at all. The response echoes the effective value in `preMs`.

actor.activeWeapon.description: The weapon wielded; absent when the wire never said.

actor.armorType.description: Armor type worn; absent when none.

actor.damage.description: Damage-log figure for this player in the event (raw family); absent without a log. On a telefrag victim: KTX's own armor+health figure (Damage.Telefrags[].bounded) when the demo carries it.

actor.health.description: Health just before the event. Absent when no stream recorded a value (stateSource absent).

actor.loc.description: Nearest named location from the map .loc file at the instant.

actor.name.description: Player display name (or the placeholder "teammate" for the party an unattributed team-kill print did not name).

actor.relation.description: Side relative to the event's actor: self (the actor), team (same team) or enemy. In an individual layout (duel, FFA) every other player is enemy.

actor.stack.description: health + armor — the telefrag ranking scalar.

actor.stateSource.description: Where the vitals came from: stream (the player's own health/armor streams) or spawn (the player had just spawned and the spawn stats had not reached the wire — the streams still read the previous life's corpse — so the vitals are the spawn state 100/0). Absent when there was no stream to read (every vital absent).

actor.survived.description: The pentagram holder a deflected teleporter died on (deflect rows).

actor.userId.description: UserID (Hub viewer link) resolved at the event's own instant.

actor.weapons.description: Tracked inventory held (the STAT_ITEMS bits the streams track).

cells.description: discharge: the discharger's cells just before firing — the discharge deals 35 × cells radius damage, so this is its magnitude. Absent when the stream has no sample.

damage.description: Damage-log total dealt to the victims (raw family); absent without a log or when none was dealt.

damageEnemy.description: Given damage to ENEMY victims in the BOUNDED family (each hit capped by the death-value rule, so a lethal radius hit counts what the victim could absorb, not the raw overkill), summed over every enemy hit — killed or not. Set on discharges; absent without a damage log.

damageTeam.description: Given damage to TEAM victims in the BOUNDED family, summed over every teammate hit — killed or not. Set on discharges; absent without a damage log.

height.description: airgib: victim feet above the floor at the hit, map units.

heightAboveAttacker.description: airgib: victim origin minus shooter origin at the hit, map units (negative = below).

quadFrags.description: quadbore: the actor's non-suicide kills between the pickup and the bore.

quadHeldMs.description: quadbore: ms since the quad pickup when the actor died; KTX quad lasts 30 000 ms, so 30000 − quadHeldMs is the quad thrown away.

sources.description: Evidence the row rests on: frags (an obituary named it) and/or damage (the damage log carried it, wire or reconstructed).

teleKind.description: telefrag: telefrag (the actor killed the victim), deflect (the actor teleported onto a pentagram holder and died — KTX dtTELE2/dtTELE3) or spawnicide (dtTELE4).

time.description: Event instant, int32 ms since match start.

victims.0.activeWeapon.description: The weapon wielded; absent when the wire never said.

victims.0.armorType.description: Armor type worn; absent when none.

victims.0.damage.description: Damage-log figure for this player in the event (raw family); absent without a log. On a telefrag victim: KTX's own armor+health figure (Damage.Telefrags[].bounded) when the demo carries it.

victims.0.health.description: Health just before the event. Absent when no stream recorded a value (stateSource absent).

victims.0.loc.description: Nearest named location from the map .loc file at the instant.

victims.0.name.description: Player display name (or the placeholder "teammate" for the party an unattributed team-kill print did not name).

victims.0.relation.description: Side relative to the event's actor: self (the actor), team (same team) or enemy. In an individual layout (duel, FFA) every other player is enemy.

victims.0.stack.description: health + armor — the telefrag ranking scalar.

victims.0.stateSource.description: Where the vitals came from: stream (the player's own health/armor streams) or spawn (the player had just spawned and the spawn stats had not reached the wire — the streams still read the previous life's corpse — so the vitals are the spawn state 100/0). Absent when there was no stream to read (every vital absent).

victims.0.survived.description: The pentagram holder a deflected teleporter died on (deflect rows).

victims.0.userId.description: UserID (Hub viewer link) resolved at the event's own instant.

victims.0.weapons.description: Tracked inventory held (the STAT_ITEMS bits the streams track).

lives.summary: Every player's lives, spawn to death
lives.description:
One row per spawn-to-death run — the natural unit of QuakeWorld
analysis — carrying the same per-interval stats block `/top-windows`
uses, plus `endReason`, `spawnLoc`, `deathLoc`, `killedBy`,
`deathWeapon`, `itemsTaken` and `weaponsHeld`.

**Segmentation & attribution.** Segmentation comes from
`streams.players[].alive` (schema v64). Two attribution rules matter
if you sum per-life stats:

- a kill made POSTHUMOUSLY — a rocket landing after its shooter died,
  measured 76-197 ms later on real demos — is credited to the life
  that fired it;
- an event on the boundary between two TOUCHING lives (a
  same-millisecond death and respawn) goes to the life that was
  ending.

`durationMs` is ALIVE time and is not extended by the posthumous
window.

**What the sums reconcile against.** Every stat here is built from the
per-event LOGS, so an unfiltered response sums, on the frag side, to
that player's `/frags` `frags[]` rows, and on the damage side to
`/damage`'s NON-SUMMARY aggregate for them. It does NOT sum:

- to `/damage`'s `events[]` rows: a telefrag or stomp folds its value
  into the totals without a per-hit row of its own, so on a demo with
  any positional kill the `events[]` sum comes in low by exactly that
  fold;
- to an unfiltered BOUNDED SUMMARY either — that response substitutes
  KTX's end-of-match scoreboard for the per-hit reconstruction these
  rows are built from;
- and not necessarily to a scoreboard aggregate such as `/frags`'
  `byPlayer`, which has other sources — a death detected from
  `DF_DEAD` / `STAT_HEALTH` with no obituary counts there and leaves
  no log row for any life to carry.

On `wipeout_3on2_red_vs_blue[q3dm6qw]` three players' per-life deaths
sum to 3/4/7 against a `byPlayer` 4/5/9, and the frag log itself holds
3/4/7 — the lives are faithful to their source.

**One demo class breaks the identity outright**, and says so by
reading zero. Where two wire slots resolve to the same player NAME,
that player's per-player stream is keyed with a `#slot` suffix while
the event logs keep the bare name, so nothing in their lives rows can
match: every stat there — kills, deaths, damage, shots — is 0, and
their pickups attach to no life at all rather than to the wrong
slot's. `/top-windows` is unaffected (its subjects come from the log
names directly).

**`deaths` is not a 0/1 flag.** It is the count of death rows
attributed to the life. It is usually 1; it is 0 whenever no frag-log
row names the player at that instant, INCLUDING on lives whose
`endReason` is `death` (four such rows on the demo above), so do not
infer one field from the other; and it can EXCEED 1, because a life
carries both the death that ended it and any death recorded during the
dead gap that followed, which is the KTX `dtTELE2` deflection
(measured across 11558 corpus lives: 12 with 2 deaths, one with 3).
Never treat it as a 0/1 flag — read `endReason` for how the life
ended.

**Rates.** Each row carries its attribution window explicitly as
`attrStart`/`attrEnd`, which is WIDER than `durationMs` (alive time
only) — divide a count by `attrEnd − attrStart` for an exact rate.

**Filtering.** `from`/`to` keep lives OVERLAPPING the window, not only
those contained; note that a filtered response does NOT reconcile —
each selected life still carries its whole attribution window, and
`minMs` drops a life together with the events in its window. They are
therefore not a response-size control either; that is `summary`. An
INVERTED window (`from` > `to`) selects nothing and returns
`lives: []`, matching `/frags`, `/damage` and `/top-windows`.

**Measuredness.** Every numeric stat is emitted even at zero; read the
envelope's `measured` block, never a field's absence, to tell an
unmeasured source from a measured zero. A demo with no damage stream
still yields lives — there, and only there, the envelope's
`dmg`/`boundedMode` echoes are absent.

**Errors.** 422 `lives_unavailable` when the demo carries no
per-player streams to segment, and equally when it has streams but
liveness was never MEASURABLE on any of them. The second case would
otherwise serve `lives: []`, which reads as "nobody ever lived" — a
different and false claim from "we could not tell".
`measured.liveness` carries the same fact on the responses that do get
served. 422 `bounded_unavailable` for an EXPLICIT `dmg=bounded` on a
demo whose bounded reconstruction was skipped; a defaulted one falls
back to `raw` and says so in `dmg`.

dmg.description:
Damage family for the on-demand damage endpoints (`/top-windows`,
`/lives`, `/top-kills`):

- `raw` — the unbound wire values;
- `bounded` — KTX-scoreboard semantics (armor absorbed + health capped
  to remaining).

Default (unset): `bounded`, falling back to `raw` on a demo whose
bounded reconstruction was skipped; an EXPLICIT `dmg=bounded` there is
a 422 `bounded_unavailable` naming the demo's `boundedMode`.

**On the interval endpoints it selects the family of the whole STATS
BLOCK**, so it applies under EVERY `/top-windows` metric and not only
the damage ones — a window picked by `metric=frags` still reports
`damageGiven`, and that number has a family. Both rules above hold
under every metric too: the skipped-demo 422 fires for an explicit
`dmg=bounded` whatever the metric, and a defaulted one falls back to
`raw` whatever the metric. On `/top-kills` it selects the family of
both `damage` and `returnDamage`, so one response is one family there
too — and since `damage` is the RANKING key, the two families can
order the list differently. The resolved family comes back as the
response's own `dmg` — read it rather than assuming the default took.

**Two values, not three:** `both` is a response SHAPE — raw fields
plus a parallel `bounded` nest, as `/damage` returns it — and these
endpoints have no such shape. One interval stats block — one kill
burst — carries one set of damage numbers, and a quantity that RANKS
has to rank on a single family, so `both` is rejected with a 400 here
for every metric and on every one of the three endpoints.

from.description: Window start, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no lower bound. Endpoints treat the window as inclusive on both ends. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

label.description: Non-secret traffic-source tag for access-log attribution. Accepted on every endpoint; never affects the response.

minMs.description: Drop lives shorter than this many integer milliseconds (default 0, keep all). Useful for filtering out spawn-frag lives.

players.description: CSV of player display names. Case-SENSITIVE (QW names are case-significant). Omit for all players. Filter semantics are per-endpoint (e.g. killer-or-victim on /frags, speaker on /chat).

summary.description:
Size control. `/lives` returns one row per spawn-to-death run and a
whole 4on4 match is ~400 of them (~240 KB), of which ~40% is per-row
collections. Note that `from`/`to` only SELECT rows here — each kept
row still carries its whole attribution window — so they are not a
size control on their own.

**What `summary=true` keeps:** EVERY ROW and every scalar (the counts,
the durations, `endReason`, `spawnLoc`/`deathLoc`,
`killedBy`/`deathWeapon`, `mainWeapon`, `weaponsHeld`).

**What it drops:** the per-row breakdown collections — `itemsTaken`,
`locs`, `eventLocs`, `victims`, `byWeapon`, `damageByWeapon`.

**One consequence to know:** `itemsTaken` is `null` on every summary
row. In a summary response that null means "not requested" and says
NOTHING about the demo — the envelope's `measured.items` remains the
authority on whether an item timeline exists. Re-ask with
`summary=false` (plus `players` / `from` / `to`) for the detail of the
lives you care about.

to.description: Window end, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no upper bound. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

attrEnd.description:
End of the attribution window. The window is the life PLUS the
dead gap that follows it (and, for the first and last lives, out
to the match edges), so that a posthumous rocket counts for the
life that fired it.

**It is wider than `durationMs`**, which measures `end − start` —
ALIVE time — and this is the one asymmetry in the row: a
per-second rate computed from a count over `durationMs` reads
HIGH — slightly when summed across a whole match, by tens of
percent on a single row where a short life is followed by a long
dead gap — while `attrEnd − attrStart` is the span the counts
actually cover.

**Truncated recordings.** On a POV or otherwise truncated
recording the final life's window can contain events its player
earned while provably still present: liveness is clipped using the
player's OWN samples, spawns and deaths, and a killer-side
obituary is deliberately not counted as presence evidence.

**Tiling.** One player's windows tile the match end to end
(half-open at exactly one side apiece), so no instant belongs to
two of them and none to none. On a demo with no match window the
last life's `attrEnd` is the int32 ceiling: there is no match end
to bound it, and everything after the last life belongs to it.

attrStart.description: Start of the ATTRIBUTION WINDOW — the span every event field in the stats block was counted over. Always present: `0` is the legitimate value on every player's first life, so an omit-on-zero rule would delete the commonest one.

damageByWeapon.description: Enemy damage given, by weapon. EXCLUDES telefrags and stomps (they carry no weapon), exactly as `/damage`'s `byWeapon` does, so this sums to at most `damageGiven` rather than to it.

damageGiven.description: To enemies. INCLUDES telefrag / stomp value, exactly as `/damage` does, so per-interval damage reconciles against that endpoint.

damageGivenSelf.description: Self damage, e.g. own rocket splash.

damageTaken.description: From ALL sources — enemy, team, self, world — and including telefrag / stomp value.

deathWeapon.description: Weapon or cause that ended the life.

deaths.description:
Death rows from the FRAG LOG naming this player as victim inside
the attribution window. Sums, over an unfiltered `/lives`
response, to that player's rows in `/frags`' `frags[]` — not
necessarily to `/frags`' `byPlayer` scoreboard, which counts
deaths the log never recorded.

**Not capped at 1 on `/lives`, and NOT a flag for `endReason`:**

- it can be 0 on a life whose `endReason` is `death` (the death
  was seen only by the `DF_DEAD` / `STAT_HEALTH` detectors and no
  obituary named it — four such rows on
  `wipeout_3on2_red_vs_blue[q3dm6qw]`);
- it can EXCEED 1, because a life carries both the death that
  ended it and any death recorded during the dead gap that
  followed (the KTX `dtTELE2` deflection — measured across 11558
  corpus lives: 12 rows with 2 deaths, one with 3).

durationMs.description:
end − start.

For a life this is ALIVE TIME ONLY, while every event field below
covers the wider attribution window (the life plus the dead gap
that follows it, so a posthumous rocket counts for the life that
fired it) — the row's `attrStart` / `attrEnd` carry that window,
so divide by `attrEnd − attrStart` for an exact rate. A rate
derived from a count and this duration therefore reads HIGH:
slightly when summed across a whole match, by tens of percent on a
single row where a short life is followed by a long dead gap.

For a top window the two coincide and there is no separate window
to publish.

endReason.description: How the life ended. `death` — a recorded death. `matchEnd` — the player was still alive. `leftGame` — the player's position track ended (they quit, or the recording lost them); liveness is clipped to observed presence, so on a truncated recording this means "the recording stopped seeing them", not "they stopped playing". Always present: an absent `killedBy` used to conflate all three.

itemsTaken.description: Every item picked up in the life's attribution window, in time order. **`null` means the demo carries no item timeline** (the same signal as `measured.items: false`); `[]` means it has one and this life took nothing. With `summary=true` it is `null` on every row regardless of the demo — there, only `measured.items` speaks.

killedBy.description: Who ended it. Absent when `endReason` is not `death`, and also on a death seen only by the health/DF_DEAD detectors with no obituary naming it — read `endReason`, not this field, to tell those apart. That second state is REACHABLE (the two detectors exist precisely because each sees deaths the other misses) but is not currently observed: across the 42 cached corpus demos, 0 of the 11364 death-ended lives — of 11558 lives in total — lack an obituary.

kills.description: Enemy kills. Suicides and teamkills excluded.

mainWeapon.description: Weapon with the most kills; ties broken by name so the value is stable.

player.description: The player whose life this is.

spawnLoc.description: Loc the life began in; absent without loc data.

team.description: Their team at match end; absent in a demo with no team labels.

teamKills.description: Teammates killed. Never scores, but shown for context.

weaponsHeld.description: Which of rl/lg/gl/ssg/sng the player held at any point while ALIVE in this life, in that order. Clipped to the alive interval, not to the attribution window: KTX does not clear the weapon bits on death, so a corpse still reads as armed. Absent means "held none of them", not "unknown".

top-kills.description:
The highlight-reel view: every enemy kill ranked by how hard the burst
that produced it hit. Neighbours — `/frags` is the exhaustive kill LOG
with no damage figure, `/damage` the whole-match aggregates plus the
per-hit log, `/top-windows` the best fixed-length stretches; this one
ranks individual KILLS.

**What a burst is.** For each enemy kill, the contiguous run of
**killing-weapon** hits the killer landed on that victim leading up to
it, summed in the requested damage family. The run is clipped below by
the start of the victim's current life.

**The burst is the KILLING WEAPON's run, and that is the question this
endpoint answers** — "how hard was this burst with this weapon".
Measured over 1,866 enemy kills, on ~8% of them that UNDERSTATES what
produced the kill: a rocket softens, a shotgun finishes, and the row
reads `weapon: sg, damage: 16` for a kill that took 250 across
weapons. Deliberate, not a defect. "What did the kill take across
weapons" stays a `/damage` question. A different-weapon hit landing
inside the run neither joins it nor breaks it.

**`gapMs` is a CAPTURE gap — narrow with `maxGapMs`, not with
`gapMs`.** The default 3000 is generous on purpose: truncation is
unrecoverable downstream while over-merge is filterable. To get the
tighter per-weapon burst your product wants, keep the rows whose
`maxGapMs` is within that weapon's cadence (LG ≈ 1200 ms, RL ≈
2300 ms) — every KEPT row then carries its gap-`g` value EXACTLY,
because dropping hits from a run only widens gaps. An over-merged row
(`maxGapMs > g`) is dropped by that filter, not truncated, and a row
outside this response's `limit` cannot re-enter — `?gapMs=g` on this
endpoint is the exact tighter walk when either matters. Lowering
`gapMs` as a display knob instead loses damage: a baked 1200 ms gap truncated 11% of rl and 23% of sg bursts,
worst measured a 291-damage triple-rocket kill reported as **2**.
`spanMs` is the DISPLAY figure ("291 dmg in 1.7 s") and is not a valid
narrowing rule — 21 of the 24 over-merged rl bursts in the corpus pass
a `span <= 2×gap` test.

**Positional kills produce no row.** A telefrag, stomp or squish
carries no damage event, so there is no run to sum and no honest
figure to rank by; they are absent from this ranking only (13 of 1,879
measured kills) and still present in `/frags` and in `/damage`'s
`telefrags` / `stomps`.

**Kills by an already-dead killer stay in**, deliberately: the walk
consults the VICTIM's liveness and never the killer's, so a rocket in
flight when its shooter died still ranks. Measured 38 of 1,866 —
posthumous rockets and mutual frags, exactly the highlights this
endpoint exists to surface.

**`returnDamage` is a value, not a flag.** It is what the victim dealt
back to this killer over the `contestedMs` window before the kill —
any weapon, same damage family. The server owns the window; the
threshold that calls a kill "contested" is yours.

**Ranking & filters.** Rows are ranked by `damage`, ties broken by the
earlier kill then by killer / victim name, so the response is stable.
`minDamage` filters on that same figure; `weapons` filters the KILLING
weapon (burst-capable tokens only: rl, lg, gl, ssg, sng, ng, sg, axe,
unknown — a positional or environmental cause cannot anchor a burst
and is rejected, not silently empty); `players`
restricts the KILLER — there is deliberately no victim-side filter,
which would be a different question. `from`/`to` bound the KILL
instant, not the burst: a kept row's run may reach back before `from`.

**Errors.** 422 `top_kills_unavailable` when the demo lacks any of the
three sources — the frag log, the damage log, or measurable liveness.
The last is not pedantry: at the 3000 ms capture gap the walk crosses
the victim's previous death on 4% of measured kills, and without the
life clip those bursts absorb the victim's PREVIOUS life. Since the
list is ranked BY damage, the contaminated rows are exactly the ones
that reach the top, and a consumer holding only this response could
not tell them apart. 422 `bounded_unavailable` for an EXPLICIT
`dmg=bounded` on a demo whose bounded reconstruction was skipped; a
defaulted one falls back to `raw` and says so in `dmg`.

contestedMs.description: The window each row's `returnDamage` sums the victim's damage back over, in integer MILLISECONDS before the kill (default 4000, max 30000). It sets the WINDOW only — `returnDamage` is a value, not a flag, so the threshold that calls a kill "contested" stays yours. Out-of-range values (below 1, including an explicit 0, or above 30000) are REJECTED with a 400 naming the range. The resolved value is echoed on the response.

dmg.description:
Damage family for the on-demand damage endpoints (`/top-windows`,
`/lives`, `/top-kills`):

- `raw` — the unbound wire values;
- `bounded` — KTX-scoreboard semantics (armor absorbed + health capped
  to remaining).

Default (unset): `bounded`, falling back to `raw` on a demo whose
bounded reconstruction was skipped; an EXPLICIT `dmg=bounded` there is
a 422 `bounded_unavailable` naming the demo's `boundedMode`.

**On the interval endpoints it selects the family of the whole STATS
BLOCK**, so it applies under EVERY `/top-windows` metric and not only
the damage ones — a window picked by `metric=frags` still reports
`damageGiven`, and that number has a family. Both rules above hold
under every metric too: the skipped-demo 422 fires for an explicit
`dmg=bounded` whatever the metric, and a defaulted one falls back to
`raw` whatever the metric. On `/top-kills` it selects the family of
both `damage` and `returnDamage`, so one response is one family there
too — and since `damage` is the RANKING key, the two families can
order the list differently. The resolved family comes back as the
response's own `dmg` — read it rather than assuming the default took.

**Two values, not three:** `both` is a response SHAPE — raw fields
plus a parallel `bounded` nest, as `/damage` returns it — and these
endpoints have no such shape. One interval stats block — one kill
burst — carries one set of damage numbers, and a quantity that RANKS
has to rank on a single family, so `both` is rejected with a 400 here
for every metric and on every one of the three endpoints.

from.description: Window start, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no lower bound. Endpoints treat the window as inclusive on both ends. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

gapMs.description:
The burst walk's CAPTURE gap, in integer MILLISECONDS (default 3000,
max 5000): a hit joins the run while it lands within `gapMs` of the
run's earliest hit so far.

**Do not lower this to get tighter bursts** — filter the response by
`maxGapMs` instead. The default is generous because truncation is
unrecoverable downstream while over-merge is filterable, and keeping
the rows with `maxGapMs <= g` gives every KEPT row its gap-`g` value
EXACTLY. A run with `maxGapMs > g` is dropped by that filter, not
truncated — the true gap-`g` walk would report its shorter suffix
instead — so the narrowed list is the gap-`g` ranking restricted to
intact runs. A baked 1200 ms gap truncated 11% of rl and 23% of sg
bursts. The parameter exists for the exact server-side recompute
(`gapMs=g` when the truncated remainders matter), not as the display
knob.

Out-of-range values are REJECTED with a 400 naming the range, never
clamped: below 1 (including an explicit `gapMs=0` — an omitted MCP
integer arrives as 0, which must not look deliberate) and above 5000,
beyond which a "burst" is two fights. The resolved value is echoed on
the response.

label.description: Non-secret traffic-source tag for access-log attribution. Accepted on every endpoint; never affects the response.

limit.description: Rows returned (default 20, max 200). A NEGATIVE value means uncapped. Out-of-range values are REJECTED with a 400, never silently clamped: an explicit `limit=0` (0 cannot mean "uncapped" — an omitted MCP integer arrives as 0, which would make a forgotten argument look deliberate) and any `limit` above the 200 maximum. The default is 20 rather than `/top-windows`' 10 because the per-weapon `maxGapMs` narrowing this endpoint expects thins the list.

minDamage.description: Drop kill bursts below this much burst damage (default 0, keep all) — the same figure the rows are ranked by, in the resolved `dmg` family. A negative value is rejected with a 400: 0 already means "no filter", since a burst's damage is non-negative.

players.description: CSV of player display names. Case-SENSITIVE (QW names are case-significant). Omit for all players. Filter semantics are per-endpoint (e.g. killer-or-victim on /frags, speaker on /chat).

to.description: Window end, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no upper bound. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

weapons.description:
CSV of weapon codes (case-insensitive). Core codes: rl, lg, gl, ssg,
sng, ng, sg, axe; on /damage the pseudo-codes tele/stomp select the
positional instant kills (which carry no real weapon).

Each endpoint validates against its OWN closed vocabulary and returns
400 `invalid_param` (listing the valid set) for an unknown token — no
more silent empty result:

- **/top-kills** filters the KILLING weapon (which is also the
  burst's own weapon) and accepts only the burst-capable subset —
  the core codes plus `unknown`. Positional (tele/stomp/squish),
  environmental and bookkeeping causes are REJECTED here: no damage
  event can anchor them, so the token would be a valid filter that
  structurally selects nothing.

`water` and `drown` are the SAME cause under the two logs' different
spellings and are accepted interchangeably wherever either is valid,
so you need not know which log backs the endpoint you are calling.

The pre-16.2 singular spelling `weapon` is an accepted legacy alias;
`weapons` wins when both are present.

damage.description: The run's summed damage in the envelope's `dmg` family — the value that ranked this row.

hits.description: How many damage events the run holds.

killer.description: Who made the kill; the frag log's name.

maxGapMs.description: The largest gap between consecutive hits in the run, `0` when `hits` is 1. This is the EXACT client-side narrowing filter: a kept row (`maxGapMs <= g`) carries its gap-`g` value verbatim; an over-merged row is dropped by the filter rather than truncated (request `gapMs=g` for the exact tighter walk).

returnDamage.description: What the victim dealt back to this killer over the `contestedMs` window before the kill: any weapon, same damage family. A value, not a flag — you own the threshold that calls a kill contested.

spanMs.description: `time` minus the run's first hit — the DISPLAY figure ("291 dmg in 1.7 s"). Not a valid rule for narrowing to a tighter gap; use `maxGapMs`.

team.description: The KILLER's team at match end; absent in a demo with no team labels.

time.description: The kill instant, match-relative ms — also the run's last hit.

victimWep.description: The victim's weapon class (`sg`|`mid`|`lg`|`rl`|`both`) at the killing hit, straight from that damage event — the same field `/damage` reports. Absent when the wire carried none.

weapon.description: The killing weapon, which IS the burst's weapon (see the endpoint description).

top-windows.summary: Each player's best stretches of the match
top-windows.description:
Top-scoring windows under one of two segmentations, chosen with
`mode`. Each has a one-sentence contract:

- `mode=fixed` (the default) — "in these `windowMs` milliseconds this
  player scored higher on `metric` than in any other stretch of the
  same length."
- `mode=gap` — "a window is a maximal run of scoring events in which
  consecutive events are no more than `gapMs` apart; its score is
  their sum."

`windowMs` is fixed mode's main knob — 5000 gives damage bursts, 30000
gives hot streaks. `gapMs` is gap mode's, is REQUIRED there and has no
default; each mode rejects the other's knob with a 400. There is
deliberately no adaptive mode with a tuning constant in it; for the
naturally variable-length unit use `/lives`, and for a fixed grid use
`/buckets`.

**Everything below applies to BOTH modes** — metric vocabulary,
ranking and the tie-break, both caps, `weapons=` scoping, `minScore`,
the stats block, measuredness and the damage family — except where the
text names `windowMs`. What gap mode changes is only where a window
starts and ends: rows are the runs themselves (so they are disjoint
per player by construction, with no overlap suppression), `end` is the
run's last event rather than `start + windowMs`, a run of one event is
a legitimate row with `durationMs` 0, and a run may span the player's
own death — `/lives` is the per-life view. See the `mode` and `gapMs`
parameters for the per-metric starting points and the rest of the
contract.

**`/top-windows mode=gap` vs `/top-kills`.** They are adjacent but not
substitutes: `/top-kills` is the per-KILL view (each row one kill plus
the killing-weapon burst that produced it, kill-anchored, clipped at
the killer's life start, with `returnDamage` and `maxGapMs`), while
gap windows are the per-STRETCH view (best sustained output, no kill
required — a 300-damage stretch with zero kills is a row — and rows
never overlap). At `metric=frags&weapons=rl&gapMs=3000` the two do
collapse onto each other, and there gap mode is the wrong tool: RL
inter-kill gaps run p50 ≈ 11.8 s, so 85% of clusters would be
singletons. Use frag gaps of 8000-15000 for multi-kill stretches, or
damage gaps around 3000 for rampages.

**`from`/`to` bound where a window may START, not what it covers** —
the one place this endpoint departs from the shared parameter
description. A window anchored at or before `to` still runs the full
`windowMs` past it, so `to=1000&windowMs=30000` returns the best
window ANCHORED in the first second, which covers up to 31 s, not
"the best window inside the first second". This is deliberate:
scoring is clipped to the same span the row reports, so a row's
`score` and its stats block always describe one identical interval.
To constrain what a window COVERS, shrink `windowMs`.

**Anchoring & shape.** Windows are anchored at REAL event times, not
a grid, so "the best 30 s" is exact rather than snapped. They are
non-overlapping per player and returned as ONE FLAT LIST, each row
carrying `player`, `team` and a 1-based `rank`.

**Ordering: `score` first, then a fixed complementary metric.** Ties
on `score` are the common case — on `metric=frags` most of a page
holds the same small integer — so rows tied on the metric are ranked
by the other half of the same moment: `damageGiven` under
`frags`/`netFrags`/`shots`/`hits`, `frags` under
`damageGiven`/`netDamage`, `damageTaken` under `deaths`, `deaths`
under `damageTaken`; then earlier start, then player name. There is
no parameter for it. The secondary is read UNSCOPED and in the
response's own damage family (the `dmg` echo), so it is exactly the
same-named field of the row's stats block — `weapons=` narrows the
score but never the tie-break. It also decides WHICH of a player's
overlapping equal-scoring candidates survives, so a window may now be
the stretch that ENDS on the scoring event rather than the one that
starts on it, when that stretch carries more of the complementary
metric. Demos with no stream for the secondary (no damage log under
`metric=frags`) simply tie at 0 and fall through to the positional
keys.

**Caps & defaults.** Two independent caps shape it:

- `perPlayer` (max windows from any one player) is applied BEFORE
  `limit` (the total), so `perPlayer=3&limit=10` means "the top 10,
  at most 3 from anyone" rather than "the top 3 of the first three
  players".
- The defaults — `limit=10`, `perPlayer=0` — make a bare call the
  match-wide top 10.

**`weapons=` and scoring.** `weapons` scopes the SCORING events only:
the stats block still describes everything that happened in the
window, so with `metric=damageGiven&weapons=lg` the `score` is a
subset of `damageGiven`. The envelope's `scoredBy` (once, not per
row — it is the same rule for every window) says which is which.
Valid weapon tokens depend on the metric's own source (the frag log
knows `hook` and `water`, the damage log `explobox` and `drown`, the
shot stream only what can be fired); `water` and `drown` are accepted
interchangeably.

- Suicides and teamkills never score, though they do appear in the
  stats block.
- Telefrags and stomps DO score, under every metric they contribute
  to: their value folds into `damageGiven`/`damageTaken` as `/damage`
  reports it and is scored on the same terms, which is why an
  UNFILTERED row's `score` equals the same-named field of its own
  stats block exactly. `weapons` is the only thing that makes the two
  diverge, and it selects positional kills too — `weapons=tele`
  scores telefrags alone.
- The one exclusion is `damageByWeapon`, matching `/damage`'s own
  `byWeapon`: a positional kill carries no wire weapon.

**Measuredness.** Every numeric stat is emitted even at zero; read
the envelope's `measured` block, never a field's absence, to tell an
unmeasured source from a measured zero.

**`dmg` — the damage family.** `dmg` selects the family of the whole
STATS BLOCK and so applies under EVERY metric, not only the damage
ones — a window picked by `metric=frags` still reports `damageGiven`.
The resolved family and the demo's reconstruction state come back on
the envelope as `dmg` and `boundedMode`, exactly as `/damage` echoes
them; read `dmg` rather than assuming the `bounded` default took,
since it silently becomes `raw` on a demo whose reconstruction was
skipped.

**Errors.** 422 `top_windows_unavailable` when the demo carries no
source stream for the chosen metric, and 422 `bounded_unavailable` —
under any metric — for an EXPLICIT `dmg=bounded` on a demo whose
bounded reconstruction was skipped. Missing loc data omits
`locs`/`eventLocs` only and never fails the request.

dmg.description:
Damage family for the on-demand damage endpoints (`/top-windows`,
`/lives`, `/top-kills`):

- `raw` — the unbound wire values;
- `bounded` — KTX-scoreboard semantics (armor absorbed + health capped
  to remaining).

Default (unset): `bounded`, falling back to `raw` on a demo whose
bounded reconstruction was skipped; an EXPLICIT `dmg=bounded` there is
a 422 `bounded_unavailable` naming the demo's `boundedMode`.

**On the interval endpoints it selects the family of the whole STATS
BLOCK**, so it applies under EVERY `/top-windows` metric and not only
the damage ones — a window picked by `metric=frags` still reports
`damageGiven`, and that number has a family. Both rules above hold
under every metric too: the skipped-demo 422 fires for an explicit
`dmg=bounded` whatever the metric, and a defaulted one falls back to
`raw` whatever the metric. On `/top-kills` it selects the family of
both `damage` and `returnDamage`, so one response is one family there
too — and since `damage` is the RANKING key, the two families can
order the list differently. The resolved family comes back as the
response's own `dmg` — read it rather than assuming the default took.

**Two values, not three:** `both` is a response SHAPE — raw fields
plus a parallel `bounded` nest, as `/damage` returns it — and these
endpoints have no such shape. One interval stats block — one kill
burst — carries one set of damage numbers, and a quantity that RANKS
has to rank on a single family, so `both` is rejected with a 400 here
for every metric and on every one of the three endpoints.

from.description: Window start, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no lower bound. Endpoints treat the window as inclusive on both ends. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

gapMs.description:
Gap mode's knob, in integer MILLISECONDS: consecutive scoring events
no more than `gapMs` apart belong to the same window.

**REQUIRED under `mode=gap`, with deliberately NO default** — omitting
it is a 400. The metrics' event cadences are too far apart for one
value to serve them: measured over the 44-demo corpus, per-player
inter-KILL gaps run p50 ≈ 11-12 s while inter-damage-event gaps run
p50 ≈ 1.0-1.1 s, so the value that reads as "a streak" on frags
dissolves damage into phase-length blobs, and the value that reads as
"a rampage" on damage leaves 85% of RL frag clusters singletons.
Requiring it also keeps the mode honest: you state what "kept doing
it" means rather than inheriting a constant nobody can justify.

**Measured starting points: ~10000 for the frag metrics
(`frags`/`deaths`/`netFrags`), ~3000 for the damage and shot
metrics.** At `metric=frags` a gap of 8000-15000 reads as a streak
(top clusters 18-22 kills); at `metric=damageGiven` a gap of
2000-3000 reads as a rampage (~900 damage over 13-21 s) and 8000
already merges whole map phases.

**Range 1..the match duration**, `windowMs`' rule exactly, and an
out-of-range value is REJECTED with a 400 naming the bound rather than
clamped. The floor covers an explicit `gapMs=0` (an omitted MCP
integer arrives as 0, which must not look deliberate) and any negative
value; the ceiling is the match duration, past which every one of a
player's events joins a single window.

**Rejected under `mode=fixed`** with a 400 — an explicit conflict, not
a silent drop, since the response echoes only its own mode's knob and
so could not show that anything was discarded.

label.description: Non-secret traffic-source tag for access-log attribution. Accepted on every endpoint; never affects the response.

limit.description:
Total windows returned across all players (default 10, max 200).
Applied AFTER `perPlayer`. A NEGATIVE value means uncapped.

Out-of-range values are REJECTED with a 400, never silently clamped: an
explicit `limit=0` (0 cannot mean "uncapped" — an omitted MCP integer
arrives as 0, which would make a forgotten argument look deliberate)
and any `limit` above the 200 maximum.

metric.description:
What a top window is ranked by — any SUMMABLE per-event quantity. Ratios (accuracy, efficiency) are deliberately absent: they do not sum, so "the best window" is undefined for them; they ride the per-window stats block instead. `netFrags` (kills − deaths) is usually what people mean by hot — five kills bought with four deaths is a trade, not a run. `deaths` finds a player's WORST stretch. Case-insensitive.
**`shots`/`hits` want a `weapons=` filter.** A "shot" is one discrete fire (an LG beam tick and a rocket each count 1), so the unfiltered sum is dominated by fast-cycling weapons; and hits are counted only for weapons whose fires LINK to damage (axe/sg/ssg/lg always, rl/gl via projectile tracking, ng/sng only when nail decoding ran), so the unfiltered figure mixes measured and unmeasured weapons. A rocket's SPLASH is a hit here — including a rocket jump's self-splash, which the stats split out as selfHits — and that is NOT KTX's rl/gl convention: KTX counts only rockets that TOUCHED a player (ktx/src/weapons.c:994, :1329) and reads ~4x lower, so never diff this against a demoinfo `acc.rl.hits`. For RL windows `metric=damageGiven&weapons=rl` is the quality signal (enemy-only by definition), while `metric=hits&weapons=lg` is the LG tracking signal (each cell counts the same; raw damage ≈ 30×hits, bounded discounts the killing cell's overkill).

minScore.description: Drop windows scoring below this many points OF THE CHOSEN METRIC (default 1) — a score threshold, not a duration; the ms-valued filter on the sibling `/lives` is `minMs`. Matters most for the net metrics, which can go negative — a window nobody would call hot. An explicit `minScore=0` is a MEANINGFUL request (keep the windows that broke even) and is honoured, not treated as "unset".

mode.description:
The SEGMENTATION — how a window's boundaries are decided (default
`fixed`, so a request written before this parameter existed is
unchanged). Case-insensitive; the resolved value is echoed on every
response, `fixed` ones included.

- `fixed` — every window is exactly `windowMs` long. "In these
  `windowMs` ms this player scored higher on `metric` than in any
  other stretch of the same length."
- `gap` — a window is a maximal run of scoring events in which
  consecutive events are no more than `gapMs` apart; its score is
  their sum. The stretch lasts as long as the player kept doing it,
  not as long as a stopwatch says. A gap of EXACTLY `gapMs` joins and
  `gapMs+1` splits; a run of one event is a legitimate window with
  `durationMs` 0.

Each mode takes exactly ONE knob and REJECTS the other's with a 400
rather than ignoring it: `gapMs` under `mode=fixed`, and `windowMs`
under `mode=gap`. `gapMs` is REQUIRED under `mode=gap` and has no
default.

Gap-mode specifics worth knowing before you read the rows:

- Signed metrics (`netFrags`, `netDamage`) cluster on ALL their
  events, negatives included — a death both extends the run and
  lowers its score. That is "net" as the fight went, and it is what
  keeps `score` equal to the same-named stat.
- A cluster MAY SPAN THE PLAYER'S OWN DEATH (kill, die, respawn, kill
  again within `gapMs` is one window). `/lives` is the per-life view.
- Clusters are disjoint per player by construction, so unlike fixed
  mode there is no overlap suppression to reason about.
- `from`/`to` still bound where a window may START — here, its first
  event; the run may end past `to`. Note the consequence on the
  `from` side: a cluster whose first event precedes `from` is not
  returned AT ALL, its post-`from` mass included — `from` never
  re-anchors a cluster. Slicing a match into `from`/`to` panes
  therefore drops straddling clusters rather than truncating them.

perPlayer.description:
Maximum windows contributed by any ONE player. Applied BEFORE `limit`,
so `perPlayer=3&limit=10` is "the top 10 with at most 3 from anyone".
Set it to spread a leaderboard across the roster; omit it for a pure
match-wide ranking in which one dominant player may own every row.

**Name-keyed.** The cap is keyed on the player NAME, so a human the
server scored as two players (a reconnect renamed `(N)<name>`) can
occupy twice the quota. `/player-stats`' `identity` is what lets you
detect that — two names, one identity; the cap itself is deliberately
left name-keyed.

**Same rule as `limit`, deliberately:** omitted is the default
(uncapped), a NEGATIVE value means uncapped, and an explicit
`perPlayer=0` is REJECTED with a 400 — an omitted MCP integer arrives
as 0, and 0 must not make a forgotten argument look like a deliberate
one.

players.description: CSV of player display names. Case-SENSITIVE (QW names are case-significant). Omit for all players. Filter semantics are per-endpoint (e.g. killer-or-victim on /frags, speaker on /chat).

to.description: Window end, match-relative integer MILLISECONDS. 0 / omitted = no upper bound. A non-integer value 400s with code `invalid_param` and an `(integer milliseconds)` hint.

weapons.description:
CSV of weapon codes (case-insensitive). Core codes: rl, lg, gl, ssg,
sng, ng, sg, axe; on /damage the pseudo-codes tele/stomp select the
positional instant kills (which carry no real weapon).

Each endpoint validates against its OWN closed vocabulary and returns
400 `invalid_param` (listing the valid set) for an unknown token — no
more silent empty result:

`water` and `drown` are the SAME cause under the two logs' different
spellings and are accepted interchangeably wherever either is valid,
so you need not know which log backs the endpoint you are calling.

The pre-16.2 singular spelling `weapon` is an accepted legacy alias;
`weapons` wins when both are present.

windowMs.description:
FIXED MODE'S knob: the window length in integer MILLISECONDS (default
30000). 5000 gives damage bursts, 30000 hot streaks, 120000 map-phase
dominance. Sweep it — there is no single right value and the API does
not pick one for you.

**Rejected under `mode=gap`** with a 400 (that mode's knob is
`gapMs`), and absent from a gap response, where a fixed length would
be a lie.

**Bounded on both sides**, and an out-of-range value is REJECTED with
a 400 naming the bound rather than clamped.

- The floor is 1 (`windowMs=0` and any negative value alike; omit the
  parameter for the default).
- The CEILING IS THE MATCH DURATION — see `/overview`'s `matchEnd` —
  because a window at least that long is simply the whole match, and a
  longer one would break the `end = start + windowMs` identity every
  row is documented by (the response would have to clamp `end`,
  leaving a `durationMs` covering time that does not exist).

damageByWeapon.description: Enemy damage given, by weapon. EXCLUDES telefrags and stomps (they carry no weapon), exactly as `/damage`'s `byWeapon` does, so this sums to at most `damageGiven` rather than to it.

damageGiven.description: To enemies. INCLUDES telefrag / stomp value, exactly as `/damage` does, so per-interval damage reconciles against that endpoint.

damageGivenSelf.description: Self damage, e.g. own rocket splash.

damageTaken.description: From ALL sources — enemy, team, self, world — and including telefrag / stomp value.

deaths.description:
Death rows from the FRAG LOG naming this player as victim inside
the attribution window. Sums, over an unfiltered `/lives`
response, to that player's rows in `/frags`' `frags[]` — not
necessarily to `/frags`' `byPlayer` scoreboard, which counts
deaths the log never recorded.

**Not capped at 1 on `/lives`, and NOT a flag for `endReason`:**

- it can be 0 on a life whose `endReason` is `death` (the death
  was seen only by the `DF_DEAD` / `STAT_HEALTH` detectors and no
  obituary named it — four such rows on
  `wipeout_3on2_red_vs_blue[q3dm6qw]`);
- it can EXCEED 1, because a life carries both the death that
  ended it and any death recorded during the dead gap that
  followed (the KTX `dtTELE2` deflection — measured across 11558
  corpus lives: 12 rows with 2 deaths, one with 3).

durationMs.description:
end − start.

For a life this is ALIVE TIME ONLY, while every event field below
covers the wider attribution window (the life plus the dead gap
that follows it, so a posthumous rocket counts for the life that
fired it) — the row's `attrStart` / `attrEnd` carry that window,
so divide by `attrEnd − attrStart` for an exact rate. A rate
derived from a count and this duration therefore reads HIGH:
slightly when summed across a whole match, by tens of percent on a
single row where a short life is followed by a long dead gap.

For a top window the two coincide and there is no separate window
to publish.

end.description: Under `mode=fixed`, `start + windowMs` (the identity holds over REST because `windowMs` is capped at the match duration; the view clamps `end` at the int32 ceiling for in-process callers, who face no such cap). Under `mode=gap` it is the run's LAST scoring event, so the row is as long as the stretch was and `end == start` on a single-event run.

kills.description: Enemy kills. Suicides and teamkills excluded.

mainWeapon.description: Weapon with the most kills; ties broken by name so the value is stable.

player.description: The player who scored in this window.

score.description: The metric total over the window — the value that selected and ranked it. WITHOUT a `weapons` filter it equals the same-named stat below exactly (telefrags and stomps score just as they fold); with one it is a SUBSET of that stat. The envelope's `scoredBy` says exactly what produced it.

team.description: Their team at match end; absent in a demo with no team labels.

teamKills.description: Teammates killed. Never scores, but shown for context.
